title: Bihar: Viral video shows three women, man consuming liquor inside Darbhanga hospital; police probe underway
content:
A viral video purportedly showing three women and a man consuming liquor inside the surgical building of Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has prompted a police inquiry, raising questions about security and discipline at the government-run healthcare institution.
The video, which surfaced on Tuesday, purportedly shows the four near a staircase inside the hospital building. The women have reportedly been described as sanitation workers, while the man has been identified as a trolley worker. However, their identities, employment status and the authenticity of the footage have not yet been officially established.
Also Read | Alcohol sold in tetra packs may mislead minors, Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response
Taking cognisance of the matter, Darbhanga senior superintendent of police (SSP) Jagunath Raddi Jalaraddi directed the Benta police station in-charge to conduct a detailed investigation.
The circulated footage purportedly shows women taking out snacks and disposable plastic glasses from a bag, followed by a man taking out a tetra pack of liquor from his waistband and handing it over.
Hindustan Times has not independently verified the video or the circumstances in which it was recorded.
Also read | Suspected phone snatcher left dangling from moving train in Bihar; video goes viral
DMCH superintendent Dr Jagdish Chandra said the footage would be examined to verify its authenticity and establish the identities of the people and the location shown in it. He said he informed the police as soon as he learnt about the alleged incident.
Chandra also said the Darbhanga district magistrate had asked him to ascertain the details and initiate appropriate action. The hospital's security in-charge, meanwhile, reportedly described the video as old.
The footage is said to be around six months old, although its date of recording has not been officially confirmed. The inquiry is expected to establish when and where the alleged incident took place and whether the people seen in the video were actually hospital employees or outsourced staff on duty.

title: ‘True character of protests exposed’: Dharmendra Pradhan attacks Rahul Gandhi over regime change remark
content: Dharmendra Pradhan criticized Rahul Gandhi for allegedly exploiting student protests to undermine India's democratic structure. He claimed these actions indicated a desire to create instability comparable to the situation in Bangladesh. In response, the Congress party maintained that their focus is on achieving a regime change through democratic elections. Ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar also contributed to the controversy surrounding the electoral process.

title: Prashant Bhushan says anti-CEC protest now a ‘fight for regime change’, BJP hits back with 'conspiracy' charge
content:
Senior Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan , who is part of the ongoing anti-CEC protests, on Friday said the agitation against alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls had become “really a fight for regime change”, drawing a sharp response from the BJP, which accused the protesters of seeking to oust the Narendra Modi government without an electoral mandate.
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi alongside Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke , student organisation leaders and activists, Bhushan said calls for regime change were part of democratic rights and that creating “disaffection” against a government was not a crime under the Constitution.
“The government alleges the opposition wants a regime change... We are currently fighting to ensure that elections are conducted properly. But if this kind of brutality continues, there will certainly be regime change.
“Yes, we all want regime change,” he said.
“What is wrong with that? BJP led several movements for regime change? Now they are saying there is a conspiracy for regime change...” Bhushan said.
“Regime change is the democratic right of every citizen. Creating disaffection for the government is not a crime as per our Constitution.
“That is why this is now really a fight for regime change against a dictatorial government. A government that is crushing democracy,” he said.
Bhushan said attempts by the authorities to suppress protests would only bring more people onto the streets. He added that young people would lead the movement for regime change, with civil society groups and political parties joining the campaign.
Also Read: 'Hope better sense prevails': No urgent direction from SC against Dipke's CP 'Tiranga' march
Defence minister Rajnath Singh accused unnamed groups of trying to use young people to foment political unrest, drawing a parallel with the events in Bangladesh.
“Attempts are being made to use the nation's youth as pawns in a politics of chaos. Some seek a regime change, modelled after the events in Bangladesh, openly admitting that they drew inspiration from the situation in Bangladesh; others, meanwhile, brazenly call for the toppling of the government. This makes it clear that their sole agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country ablaze...their struggle is not for electoral reform, nor is it about SIR or Gyanesh Kumar; it is not for the sake of a bright future for the nation's youth, rather, it is a conspiracy to seize power by inciting anarchy in the country...”
BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan said Bhushan’s remarks proved that the SIR process was a “smokescreen” for the opposition’s alleged agenda to bring down the government.
“The toxic and venomous rant by Prashant Bhushan demanding a regime change in India goes to prove beyond doubt that for Rahul Gandhi and his vile ecosystem, the SIR process was just a smokescreen. The ulterior motive and hidden anarchic agenda of Rahul Gandhi and his cohorts have always been to derail Indian democracy and somehow seize power in an undemocratic manner...” Kesavan said.
Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis also reacted to Bhushan’s remarks, posting: “It’s done bro, everything is exposed !! Afterall, it was all about ‘Regime Change’..”
BJP leader CT Ravi said Bhushan’s statement raised questions about the motives behind the agitation seeking the CEC’s resignation. He said allegations of SIR irregularities and “vote chori” could not substitute for an evidence-based debate, and argued that street protests could not override the government’s democratic mandate.
BJP's National Spokesperson Guruprakash Paswan said, "Prashant Bhushan openly talks about “regime change.” In a democracy, governments are changed by the people through elections, not through street anarchy and political unrest".
BJP MP Sambit Patra said Bhushan’s statement confirmed the party’s claim that the agitation was aimed at changing the government rather than addressing electoral reforms.
“This country is not anyone’s private property. It does not belong to any single family. It belongs to 1.4 billion people,” Patra said, alleging that the opposition wanted to seize power without contesting elections.
“Our Constitution provides a clear process for changing a government. Elections are held in this country every five years, allowing people to exercise their right to vote. These are the legitimate channels through which a change in power can occur. But you do not believe in this process. You believe in chaos; you believe in anarchy,” he said.

title: Dhruv Rathee not arrested: Noida Police calls social media posts on YouTuber false
content:
Police in Uttar Pradesh's Noida on Friday refuted social media claims alleging the arrest of Germany-based YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, describing the information as completely false, misleading and baseless.
Notably, since Friday morning, several users have been posting on X, speculating that Dhruv Rathee was arrested by Noida Police and sharing a video to support the claim.
In a fact-check clarification, the police stated that " Dhruv Rathee has not been arrested by Noida Police."
The clarification comes after several social media handles reportedly circulated posts claiming that the YouTuber had been taken into custody.
Appealing to the public, Noida Police urged people not to circulate misleading or unverified messages. It also advised social media users to verify the authenticity of information before sharing it online.
The police further warned that individuals found spreading false information, misleading content or rumours could face strict legal action under the applicable laws.
“The general public is appealed not to disseminate such misleading and unverified messages, and to always verify the authenticity of any information before sharing it. Strict legal action will be taken as per prevailing legal provisions against individuals disseminating misleading, false, or rumor-mongering content,” the X post on the handle of Police Commissionerate Gautam Buddh Nagar read.
The speculation comes days after the YouTuber was released after nearly 18 hours after detaining him from his residence in Sector 56 of Haryana's Gurugram.
He was detained on Sunday for allegedly planning to protest irregularities in electoral rolls at Jantar Mantar, where prohibitory orders were enforced, an officer said.
Police said the 32-year-old social media activist was kept under watch at one of the offices of the crime branch in Gurugram, from where he was handed over to his family members around 3 am on Sunday, HT earlier reported.
“Yes, he has been set free. His family members arrived to receive him at a crime branch office where he was kept detained, ” a senior officer was quoted as saying.
“He was released after discussion with Delhi police, and it was ensured that he won’t be a part of a group or mob trying to create law and order problems where prohibitory orders were already in force,” the officer said.
Police said that he was detained under Section 172(2) (detain or remove any person who resists, refuses, ignores, or disregards a lawful direction) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

title: Palakkad mob lynching: Chennithala condemns killing, 7 arrested
content:
Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala on Friday strongly condemned the alleged mob lynching of an unidentified man in Palakkad district, saying seven people have been arrested and an SIT will probe the incident.
Replying to a submission in the state Assembly, Chennithala termed the incident "extremely brutal and condemnable", saying such cruelty could not be accepted in a progressive state like Keralam, which has achieved complete literacy and implemented progressive legislation.
He said a 10-member SIT has been constituted for further investigation and assured the House that no one involved in the crime will be spared.
The deceased was estimated to be aged between 35 and 40, but his identity was yet to be established, the minister said.
Chennithala said he had directed the ADGP to seek the assistance of his Tamil Nadu counterpart to identify the victim, as the incident occurred in a village bordering the neighbouring state.
Describing the killing as inhuman and heinous, the minister said the victim's body bore around 52 injuries.
"How can we justify a group of people joining together to commit such an inhuman and heinous murder?" he asked.
The incident came to light after the man's body was found near the Moolathara dam, close to Meenakshipuram, by residents on Sunday morning.
Police initially registered a case of unnatural death. However, examination of CCTV footage and the emergence of fresh evidence revealed that a group of people had allegedly attacked the man, pelting stones at him and beating him with wooden sticks, Chennithala said.
Subsequently, charges including murder were invoked against the accused, he added.
According to the minister, it was alleged that the victim had exposed himself in front of some local women, provoking the accused to attack him.
However, he said, there were law-enforcement agencies and courts to deal with such matters, and no one can be permitted to take the law into their own hands by attacking and killing a person.
A post-mortem examination conducted at Thrissur Medical College Hospital had revealed signs of murder, police said earlier.
The man had reportedly been roaming around the village in the Keralam-Tamil Nadu border region for some time, but his identity remained unknown.
The incident, which allegedly occurred on Saturday, has sent shockwaves through the district. It is the third alleged mob lynching reported in Palakkad in recent years.
Recalling the 2018 lynching of Madhu, a 27-year-old tribal youth from Chindakki Ooru in Attappadi, Chennithala said the incident remained a grim reminder of mob violence.
Madhu was allegedly beaten to death by a mob after being accused of stealing rice and other grocery items from a shop.
In another incident in December 2025, five people were arrested for allegedly beating a native of Chhattisgarh to death on suspicion of theft within the limits of the Walayar police station.

title: Malegaon court awards death sentence to man convicted of raping, murdering 4-year-old girl
content:
A Malegaon court on Friday sentenced Vijay Khairnar to death for the sexual assault and murder of a four-year-old girl in Dongrale village in Maharashtra 's Nashik district in November 2025, with the court terming the crime a ‘rarest of rare’ case.
Special public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said the court had considered the gravity of the crime and the circumstantial evidence establishing Khairnar’s involvement while deciding the sentence. The court did not consider the convict’s poverty and illiteracy as grounds for leniency, he said.
“The prosecution examined 24 witnesses during the trial. The judgment runs into 225 pages. Along with the intensity of the crime, there was circumstantial evidence to establish his involvement,” Nikam said.
He added that the prosecution hoped the Bombay high court and the Supreme Court would dispose of the case expeditiously so that the sentence could be carried out.
The case relates to the incident on November 16, 2025, when the girl went missing while playing near her home in Dongrale village in Malegaon taluka. Her body was subsequently found in a nullah near a mobile tower. Investigators alleged that Khairnar, then 24, lured the child with chocolate before sexually assaulting and killing her.
Khairnar, a daily-wage worker and resident of the area, was arrested on the day of the incident. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, DNA test results and other material to establish his involvement, despite the absence of direct eyewitnesses or CCTV footage.
A chargesheet was filed on January 26, 2026, and the case was heard by a fast-track court. The court accepted the prosecution's case and convicted Khairnar before sentencing him to death on Friday.
The death sentence will be subject to confirmation by the Bombay high court, as required by law.

title: 1980 murder case: Allahabad HC finds two convicts were minors, remits matter to Juvenile Justice Board
content:
Lucknow, The Allahabad High Court has set aside the sentences of two men convicted in a murder case 46 years ago after finding that both were minors at the time of the crime.
However, the Lucknow bench of the court upheld their conviction and referred the matter to the Juvenile Justice Board to determine the appropriate punishment.
A division bench of Justices Abdul Moin and Pramod Kumar Srivastava on Thursday passed the order on an appeal arising from the incident that took place in Sultanpur on September 28, 1980.
According to the prosecution, eight men attacked several persons with sharp-edged weapons and spears.
Four people - Shamshad, Abdul Rafiq, Dilsher and Hamidullah - were killed in the incident, while several others sustained injuries.
The sessions court had convicted all eight accused and sentenced them to life imprisonment on December 14, 1981.
During the pendency of their appeal in the high court, appellants Siraj Ahmad and Abdul Wahid claimed that they were minors when the incident occurred.
Following the high court's directions, the Juvenile Justice Board conducted an inquiry to ascertain their age.
Based on the board's report and educational records, the court found that Ahmad was 17 years and 10 months old, while Wahid was 17 years and 11 months old at the time of the crime.
While upholding their conviction, the bench observed that the testimonies of injured eyewitnesses and other witnesses were consistent with the medical evidence.
The prosecution had successfully established the charges, and there were no grounds to interfere with the findings of guilt.
However, the bench held that the sentences imposed under the criminal law could not be sustained in view of their juvenile status at the time of the offence.
The court observed that the two convicts could not be let off without any consequence, but the appropriate order had to be passed in accordance with the provisions of the juvenile justice law.
The bench directed both men to appear before the Juvenile Justice Board on October 28 along with a certified copy of the judgment. The board has been asked to pass an appropriate order within six weeks of receiving the certified copy.

title: Pinarayi Vijayan moves SC against HC order to lodge FIR in CMRL bribery case
content:
New Delhi, Former Keralam chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday moved the Supreme Court challenging a High Court of Kerala order to register an FIR in the alleged CMRL bribery case.
Sidharth Luthra, appearing for Vijayan, mentioned the plea for urgent listing before a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi, saying an FIR has been registered in the case.
Luthra also urged the bench to grant Vijayan protection from coercive action.
The CJI said the matter would be heard when the apex court re-opens on October 26 after the Dussehra break.
The CJI also said he may constitute a bench during the holidays next week, subject to the availability of judges.
In a setback to Vijayan and his kin, the Kerala High Court on Thursday dismissed their pleas to file appeals against a single-judge direction to lodge an FIR against them in the alleged CMRL bribery case.
A division bench of the high court rejected the applications of Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P A Mohamed Riyas to file an appeal against the single judge's October 9 order, while holding that "an accused in a corruption case has no legal right to be heard before registering the FIR".
It said that since the applications are dismissed, their appeals are also dismissed consequently.
Vijayan, Veena and Riyas, in their appeals before the division bench, had claimed that they were not heard by the single judge before issuing the October 9 direction to lodge the FIR.
The high court on October 9 directed the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to register a case based on a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate to the state police.
The ED had sought registration of a case based on evidence gathered during its investigation and searches conducted under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
The agency has alleged that Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited made fraudulent payments of ₹ 2.78 crore to Veena's now-defunct company, Exalogic Solutions, under the guise of IT consultancy services.

title: Rajnath Singh attacks Congress over anti-CEC protests: ‘Conspiracy to grab power’
content:
Union defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday attacked the Opposition Congress over protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll, saying they raise serious questions. He accused the Opposition of wanting to push youth into anarchy to grab power.
“This fight is not for electoral reforms, not for SIR, not against Gyanesh Kumar, not for bright future of youth. It is a conspiracy to grab power. In democracy there is no licence to spread anarchy and attack constitutional institutions,” Singh said in Lucknow .
Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets seeking Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of SIR even as authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress. Many protesters were dragged, manhandled and detained as the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) blamed the Opposition for trying to deflect attention from its electoral failures.
Singh said institutions are being defamed and called it political opportunism. “Rahul Gandhi should do introspection. This is my suggestion. We have chosen a path of dialogue, not confrontation, for nation building,” he said.
He referred to the state of Emergency in the 1970s and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as unpardonable crimes under the Congress patronage. He also cited the Congress’s role in saving the Samajwadi Party government after the 1990 firing on volunteers who converged on Ayodhya as part of the Ram temple campaign.
Singh said the Congress is committing the fourth unpardonable crime by hurting the Constitution, constitutional values and institutions. “In 1975 [Prime Minister] Indira Gandhi put democracy behind bars [during the state of Emergency]. Today Rahul Gandhi keeps the Constitution in his pocket and tries to spread anarchy,” Singh said.
He accused the Congress of making the Election Commission of India (ECI) its puppet. “There was a recommendation to remove Naveen Chawla as an election commissioner [in 2009] over the allegation that he shared information with Congress. Congress elevated him to the post of the chief election commissioner.”
Singh said the Congress made former chief election commissioner MS Gill Union minister twice. “Until 1993, elections were held without voter IDs. Before 1993, there was no voter ID. There was no solid proof to establish voter identity. Since voter IDs were introduced, a majority has become a distant dream for Congress. Since the voter ID system was implemented, Congress has never formed a government,” he said.
The minister cited Congress’s vote theft allegation and said it won in the Uttar Pradesh assembly election last in 1985. “Congress has not got a majority since 1984, when BJP was a two-seat party. Was this vote theft or failure to work? Rahul Gandhi should answer.”
Singh said they never doubted constitutional institutions. “We never doubted the electoral system. We never misled people by defaming institutions. We always respected people, the Constitution and constitutional institutions,” Singh said. He said Congress has been out of power in Uttar Pradesh for the last 37 years. “Is this vote theft or failure to work? I want to ask Rahul Gandhi, can you win the Rae Bareli seat without the Samajwadi Party?”
He accused Rahul Gandhi of practising politics of disruption. “Democracy does not give licence to unleash violence,” he said, citing a Supreme Court observation on Thursday.

title: Ammo deal graft probe casts shadow on top-performing defence PSU, clean-up on cards
content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into an alleged corruption case linked to a ₹ 500-crore ammunition contract has cast a shadow over Munitions India Limited (MIL), one of the defence ministry’s best-performing ordnance units which has also strengthened its presence in overseas markets.
MIL is set to face a clean-up and a renewed push for accountability following the corruption allegations, officials familiar with the matter said. The department of defence production is tracking the case closely, the officials added.
MIL executive director Anil Kumar, his brother B Harshavardhan and SMPP Limited CEO Ashish Kansal were arrested on Wednesday.
Also Read: CBI to examine all recent contracts awarded by arrested official amid ₹ 500 crore ammunition deal bribery case
According to official data, MIL posted a profit after tax of ₹ 1,250 crore in 2025-26, the highest among the seven defence companies carved out of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) five years ago.
The seven firms, including Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited, Troop Comforts Limited, India Optel Limited, Avani Armoured Vehicles, Gliders India Limited and Yantra India Limited, together posted a profit of ₹ 2,801 crore, the data shows.
MIL reported record revenue of ₹ 10,954 crore in 2025-26, up 33% from the previous year. The Pune-headquartered company manufactures a wide range of ammunition, including tank ammunition, bombs and rockets. It has secured export orders worth ₹ 1,500 crore for 28 products across nine countries.
The OFB’s corporatisation was aimed at boosting its efficiency and competitiveness in a long-awaited reform in the country’s defence manufacturing sector.
SMPP Limited could face suspension or a ban on government business dealings under the Centre’s rules for procuring weapons and systems following the graft charges, as HT first reported. The department of defence production is expected to decide on possible action against the firm. SMPP manufactures ammunition, loitering munitions, bullet-proof jackets and helmets.
The Defence Procurement Manual states that the competent authority may impose financial penalties and/or suspend or ban business dealings with an entity if it resorts to corrupt practices, unfair means , or illegal activities at any stage to secure a contract, even when a PCIP (pre-contract integrity pact) is not mandated.
Violation of the PCIP is also a key ground for initiating action.
The manual adds that the competent authority may suspend business dealings with an entity pending a full inquiry into allegations or facts relating to any ground for punitive action. The government may suspend business dealings with an entity when it refers any complaint against it to the CBI or any investigating agency or when it receives intimation regarding the initiation of a criminal investigation or inquiry against any entity.
The period of suspension ordinarily does not exceed one year. In exceptional cases and those involving national security, the government may order a longer ban.

title: Manipur: Kuki body demands probe into killing of woman in Kamjong district
content:
Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), a Kuki Zo body, on Friday condemned the killing of a woman of the community allegedly by cadres of National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Issac Muivah (NSCN-IM) faction in Manipur’s Kamjong district a day earlier and demanded an impartial investigation into the incident.
According to a statement issued by KZC, four Kuki-Zo villagers were travelling from Molvailup to Phaikoh to purchase essential commodities when they were reportedly ambushed by NSCN-IM cadres at around 4pm on Thursday.
During the incident, one Hatneikim Haokip, was killed at the spot, while her husband, identified as Jamkhogam Haokip, sustained serious injuries, the council said.
The council claimed that the incident brought the reported death toll of Kuki-Zo civilians killed in the violence attributed to NSCN-IM and Zeliangrong United Front- Kamson [ZUF(K)] faction to 30. The council demanded an immediate and impartial investigation to book those responsible for the act.
Also Read: Kuki Man found dead after alleged abduction by armed group in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district
“If Naga leaders in Manipur are demanding the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreements with KNO/UPF, the ceasefire arrangement with NSCN -IM must also be reviewed for abrogation. The same standards must apply to all armed groups, without discrimination or political favouritism,” the KZC said in the statement.
“The government must uphold the rule of law through consistent and impartial action. It cannot apply different standards to different groups while overlooking allegations of grave violence against the Kuki-Zo people. Justice cannot be selective, and accountability must be equal for all,” Kuki-Zo Council said.
